intervals.label: engineering run with a 4 g prototype
intervals.note: Year precision for the start ("late 2014"); the end is the full sensor upgrade in "mid 2016" (next interval). The engineering run paper (arXiv:1604.01343) reports the first year of operation of the 4 g prototype.
intervals.quote: The engineering prototype of the experiment was installed at the reactor site in late 2014

intervals.label: data taking with the upgraded CCD array
intervals.note: Open-ended: later papers report 2019 data and a skipper-CCD update (2021-22, conference abstract only), and the 2022 paper says the experiment "is taking data". No source consulted states that data taking has ended.
intervals.quote: A complete upgrade of the sensors was performed in mid 2016

placements.note: Campus-grade plant point; the container position is not published.
placements.quote: in a temporary laboratory space, built inside a standard shipping container located outside of the main reactor building

active_mass.quote: considering an active mass 47.6 g (8 CCDs)

summary.plain: A cooled array of silicon camera sensors, so quiet that a single nuclear recoil of about a thousand electronvolts shows up, inside a thick lead and polyethylene shield.
summary.technical: Cryogenic array of low-noise fully depleted scientific CCDs (readout noise < 2 e- RMS) in a vacuum vessel inside a 30 cm polyethylene / 15 cm lead / 30 cm polyethylene shield; 8 CCDs analysed in 2016 and 2019; skipper-CCDs added in 2021.

technology.quote: The Coherent Neutrino-Nucleus Interaction Experiment (CONNIE) uses low-noise fully depleted charge-coupled devices (CCDs)
technology.value: Array of low-noise fully depleted charge-coupled devices (CCDs) operated cryogenically
